I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou, that is what fits my soil, water, machinery, and labor best, and it is the safest way for me to keep steady grain output. I will grow winter wheat first, then follow with summer maize on the same land. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is stable and easier for me to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is better and the return is usually worth it. For wheat, I will prepare the land with ploughing, put most of the phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, split the nitrogen, irrigate at the key stages, and spray only when disease, weeds, or insects become a real problem. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into maize with no-tillage seeding so I do not lose moisture or time. I will give maize enough nitrogen for strong growth, keep fertilizer practical, irrigate a couple of times if rain is not enough, and control weeds and borers with limited but timely spraying. My goal is not fancy management. I will do the work that is most reliable, keeps costs under control, and gives me stable yield.
